# Independent root audit of intrinsic half-depth rigidity

Audited `candidate b90a2673d60a00b3` in full.
Result: PASS. This is an auxiliary characterization and does not prove OC.

## Angular injectivity and boundary mass

The Gaussian/Hermite proof applies to arbitrary finite signed angular
measures, including atoms and measures on subspheres. The conditional
Gaussian generating-function calculation is exact. For odd degree 2k+1,
the coefficient is 2 phi(0) H_(2k)(0), nonzero, including k=0. Gaussian
polynomial integrability justifies Fubini. Vanishing of all directional
homogeneous odd polynomial integrals implies every odd monomial integral
vanishes by polynomial coefficient identification. Evenness then follows
from real Stone-Weierstrass on the sphere, also when ambient dimension is
one and the sphere has two points.

For q>0 the original source gives no mass to the center. Fubini over
Gaussian normals therefore proves that almost every through-center
boundary is null, even when exceptional boundaries contain full fibers.
The hypothesized ALL closed-cap bound yields equal halves on these
generic boundaries. Conversely angular evenness gives the correct closed
hemisphere bound INCLUDING all exceptional boundary mass. Thus the proof
does not discard the halfspaces required by OC.

## Lattice rays and intrinsic measure

Every nonzero integer difference from j has a unique positive integer
multiple representation on one oriented primitive ray. Different ray
strata in the sphere are disjoint Borel sets. Their charts have the
continuous inverse s=|v| theta_x/|theta_z|, so equality of chart pushforwards
legitimately implies equality of the pulled-back finite measures.
Scaling a fiber by 1/k gives exactly the weight k^q in that pullback.
No surface Jacobian is missing, because both sides use the SAME chart.

The actual point y in C supplies the prefix nesting at every intervening
integer base. A positive q-dimensional farther fiber forces all earlier
ones on its ray to have positive q-volume. On each side those positive
fibers share one affine q-plane by containment. Equality of positive
measures forces the two planes to coincide, because distinct affine
q-planes intersect only in an H_q-null set. Only after this argument does
the proof compare density indicators relative to a common H_q measure.

Strict increase of sum_(k<=r) k^q recovers each prefix and every positive
fiber. Equality almost everywhere of full relative-dimensional closed
convex sets implies their exact equality by the relative interior-ball
argument stated in the note. Null fibers need not be equal and no equality
of the whole mixed set is inferred from measure symmetry.

## Own fiber and all dimensions

A recovered reflected positive pair has midpoint difference body
containing a relative q-ball around c; thus it forces a positive own
q-fiber. If no such pair exists, all positive mass is already in the own
fiber. This settles possible lower-dimensional initial center fibers.
The polar formula rho^q/q is valid about a boundary point of a convex set
as well, with zero radial extent in missing directions. For q=1 it uses
the two-point surface measure and has the same factor. Its evenness gives
equality up to q-volume null sets and then exact convex-set equality.

When n=0, there are no nonzero integer rays and the own-fiber argument
alone proves the assertion. The stated q=0 example correctly fails:
closed halfspaces at a counted atom can have depth one half without
angular balance. All claimed positive-dimensional cases are covered.

## Exact ambient thickening

For E=C intersect (2y-C) with positive H_q mixed mass, a positive fiber
and its reflected partner force a positive own q-fiber. If pi(E) is
full-dimensional, symmetry puts j in its interior. The stated segment
argument shows that an interior projection point of an ambient convex
body has an interior lift: choose an interior lift at another base,
continue its base segment past j within pi(C), and take the corresponding
strict convex combination. Thus q=d. A positive own d-fiber plus n
independent base directions makes E full-dimensional.

Consequently a deficient E has proper base affine span A. There are only
finitely many integer bases in pi(C), so their positive distances outside
A have a positive minimum. An interior ball sufficiently close to y can
be placed in a strict halfspace whose boundary contains A. Its projected
distance from A is below that minimum. The convex hull with E has no
integer bases outside A and has exactly E's slices at every base in A:
any positive ball weight has strictly positive separating functional.
This proves exact preservation of the ENTIRE mixed set while making an
actual ambient body. In particular, no limit or mass leakage is hidden.

The extraction equivalence uses H_q consistently because a subbody of C
cannot have a higher-dimensional integer fiber, and positive H_q mass
forces its maximal fiber dimension to equal q. Its local condition is
HALF-depth. The note correctly identifies this with gamma_d only when
d=1, and makes no gamma_d conclusion for higher d.
